en: Steam causes worse burns than boiling water because condensing steam releases extra heat energy into the skin.
Boiling water kills harmful bacteria, but filtering it through a clean cloth removes larger physical dirt particles.
Never mix bleach with vinegar because combining these liquids creates a toxic chlorine gas that damages your lungs.
Sunscreen protects your skin by absorbing or reflecting harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun before it damages cells.
Rubbing alcohol feels cold on your skin because it evaporates quickly, absorbing heat energy from your body.
Drinking seawater dehydrates you because your kidneys must use more water to excrete the excess dissolved salt.
Leaving aerosol spray cans in a hot car increases the gas pressure inside, which can cause the can to explode.
Melting chocolate is a physical change because you can solidify it again by cooling it without altering its chemical composition.
Crushing a delayed-release medicine pill destroys its protective coating, causing the drug to enter your bloodstream too quickly.
Pure water is a poor electrical conductor, but dissolved impurities like sweat make it dangerous around electricity.
Never touch dry ice with bare hands because its extremely low temperature causes severe frostbite within seconds.
Soap cleans grease off your hands because its molecules bind to both water and oil, washing the dirt away.
